modules.purpose:
Prepare one river-backbone product from declared inputs, then audit it cold.

This tool is **scheduling and I/O only**. The gates, the segmentation, the per-quantity
completeness and the side-input contracts belong to
``terrain_pipeline.surface_rivers.metric_backbone_precompute``; the product format belongs
to ``terrain_pipeline.surface_rivers.metric_backbone_product``. Nothing algorithmic lives
here.

Flow, in this order and no other
--------------------------------
1. the support is **declared before any page is read**: world seed, 30 m spacing, signed
   native origin, ``shape_zx``, the plan version and the cell budget;
2. the pinned TD pages are read through ``native_30m_source.load_native_window`` with their
   SHA256 pins, so real pages are read and hashed rather than trusted;
3. the B1 parent is rebuilt through ``metric_world_domains.domain_candidates`` and its
   identity must equal the pinned evidence identity -- a rebuild that drifts is refused
   before any backbone exists;
4. the flux quantities are loaded from **explicit** inputs only (a declared event model or
   a declared climatology estimate); there is no built-in climate estimator, and a missing
   input becomes ``not_available_pending`` rather than zero;
5. the backbone is built and written into a hidden partial directory;
6. a **separate process** runs ``tools/audit_river_backbone.py`` against that partial
   directory;
7. only a PASS is renamed into the requested output path. A failure keeps the partial
   evidence under a ``*.rejected*`` name and the output path stays absent, so a failing run
   can never leave something that looks like a product.

The formal product target is ``artifacts/river-backbone-precompute-v1/``; this tool
defaults to the scratch staging directory and refuses to write under ``artifacts/`` unless
``--allow-artifact-target`` is passed **and** the audit passed in the same run.

modules.purpose:
Read-only query of one prepared river-backbone product.

This tool answers questions from an already published product directory. It never routes,
never re-derives D8, never fills a depression and never re-accumulates discharge: a load
verifies bytes, budget, headers, identity and the internal coherence of the stored arrays,
and the query then indexes those stored arrays.

Scope
-----
``census``            counts, declared gates, quantity list, hydraulic availability
``reach``             one reach row plus its ordered native trace
``cell``              one world cell: area, area status, geometry, quantities
``scope``             one named read scope through the same index

Refusals are specific
---------------------
A point outside the support, a point that does not land on a cell reference point, an
unresolved cell, a cell outside the prepared channel, an undeclared quantity and anything
this product does not contain (water depth, stage, hydraulics, a natural outlet, a
permanent terminal) are all refused by name, never answered with a zero or a blank.

modules.purpose:
Synthetic orthophoto-style rendering of a saved world reach.

What this is
------------
A **visualisation** that imitates an overhead remote-sensing image. It is not
satellite data: no observation, sensor model or spectral calibration is
involved. Surface colour, hillshade and water tint are declared rendering
choices; the elevation field, carved bed and water stages come from saved
physical results.

Declared rendering choices (also written into the report)
--------------------------------------------------------
* Sun azimuth 315 deg, altitude 45 deg, constant. This is a drawing light, not
  an observation and not a solar-geometry computation.
* Elevation colour bands and the slope-to-rock blend are aesthetic.
* Water colour maps depth; it is not a spectral water index.

Physical quantities read from the saved run
------------------------------------------
``source-owner-left/right.npz``  real 10 km coarse terrain pages of the owning
                                 cores (identical in their overlap),
``generated-geometry.npz``       carved bed on the 50 m conforming mesh,
``dynamic-water-sediment-bed.npz`` per-interval node volume and node bed.

Run
---
    python tools/render_remote_sensing.py \
        --run .scratch/cross-region-tributary/real-world-run-03 \
        --output .scratch/cross-region-tributary/real-world-run-03/remote-sensing

modules.purpose:
Render an offline terrain map in remote-sensing or topographic style.

Two declared cartographic styles, both built from ``terrain_pipeline.terrain_map_style``:

``remote``
    Continuous hypsometric tint under physical relief shading, with the routing network
    drawn as permanent (solid) and seasonal (dashed) channels.  The look of a shaded-relief
    satellite composite: no graticule, because a grid is a printed-sheet device, not imagery.
``topo``
    Discrete hypsometric bands, index contours on every band edge, a kilometre graticule,
    scale bar and north arrow.  The look of a printed topographic sheet.

Where the data comes from
-------------------------
``--source``  a routed terrain archive holding ``original_td_m`` plus a ``receiver`` and
              optional ``permanent_channel_mask`` / ``seasonal_channel_mask``.
``--bundle``  a special-terrain surface bundle holding ``surface_xyz_m``; the chart is used
              *as stored*, and the figure is labelled a synthetic geometry study because a
              chart is not a georeferenced landscape.

What this tool refuses to do
----------------------------
* Write anywhere under ``verification/``.
* Draw a degree graticule unless the caller declares the metres-per-degree conversion
  explicitly; this terrain is an unbounded tile-pixel field, not a sphere.  Even then the
  figure stamps ``declared_graticule_not_a_projection`` and marks the labels with ``*``.
* Certify anything.  Every report carries ``status=candidate`` plus the four capability
  flags read from the source, and the figures are illustrations of stored arrays.

Colour limits and the grid step are derived from the chart unless the caller overrides them: a
208 m karst chart keeps the 536 m large-TD scale only if you ask for it, and a 160 m chart gets
a 20 m grid rather than a 10 km one that would draw nothing.  The one exception is the default
large-TD source, which keeps the frozen ``ELEVATION_LIMITS`` used by the existing review tools
so that a new map can be laid beside an old one without re-learning the scale.

modules.purpose:
Two-dimensional floodplain / terminal-basin run fed by the solved reach.

What this does
--------------
Takes the finished one-dimensional reach of `full-reach-run-02` and drives a
two-dimensional local-inertial march (the frozen
`regional-surface-local-inertial-D4-implicit-new-q-drag-v2` solver, unchanged) over a
window of the TD 30 m fine terrain field.

Coupling direction: **one way, 1D -> 2D**. Water enters the two-dimensional domain
only where a reach edge crosses the window boundary, on that boundary cell, using the
donor node's own saved `water_outgoing_volume_m3`. Nothing flows back. Every injected
cubic metre is a line item the reach ledger already removed from the donor, so the
two-dimensional ledger closes on its own and no volume is counted twice.

Run
---
    python tools/run_floodplain_2d.py \
        --output .scratch/cross-region-tributary/floodplain-2d-01

`solve_sediment` nodal recoupling (`world_channel_dynamics.couple_nodal_reach`), and
the terminal open-outflow volume feeds the existing `metric_lake_storage` level-pool
store (`world_reach_lake`).

Geometry feasibility is a real constraint of the old canonical carver: it rejects a
centreline edge whose bilinear source profile is not strictly monotone
(`metric_channel_geometry._route_slope`, "candidate has uphill original-bed
 derivative"). The same guard is reused here, edge by edge, instead of being
re-implemented. A refused edge truncates the reach there; its upstream subtree
enters through an explicit, fully specified boundary hydrograph produced by the same
soil bucket over the omitted cells, so reach plus declared scenarios still carry the
whole basin volume.

modules.purpose:
Read-only p5.3 distribution run: are all 16 biome palette slots reachable?

Contract: ``.scratch/river-infinite-world/biome-climate-spec.md``.

Labels used throughout (they are kept apart on purpose):

* **marginal edge** -- a distribution measured on **one grid** for **one axis**: the
  landform ordinals on the published ``literal_metre`` artifact, and the climate
  variants on a grid covering a full latitude period.
* **co-located joint observation** -- on **one and the same grid**, how many of the
  16 ``(ordinal, variant)`` slots actually occur together.  That is what a world
  can show inside a single window; it is reported for the published 15.27 km
  window and for a large grid spanning one latitude period.
* **direct-product reachability** -- ``{(ordinal, variant)}`` of the two measured
  marginal edges, mapped through ``palette_index`` to the 16 frozen palette names.
  This says the 16 slots are *addressable*, **not** that 16 slots were observed on
  one grid.

The acceptance grid is 12 columns x 96 rows over x 0..880 km and z 0..one whole
latitude period (1 920 km), which is §7.1's ">= 1 complete latitude period".  The contract's
§6.1 probe lattice (1 900 km = 0.99 periods, deliberately stopping short of the seam) is
re-run only to reproduce that probe's published share table, and the period-coverage claim
is kept on the 1 920 km grid alone.  A denser 24 x 192 cross-check grid, a five-phase
robustness sweep of the z origin, and a precipitation-saturation lattice sweep are run as
well.

The two axes move on different scales (contract §6.3, measured): the landform
ordinal ``dominant_type`` changes within ~15 km of terrain while the climate
``variant`` needs one full ``LATITUDE_PERIOD_M`` (1 920 km) to walk a period.  On
the published 15.27 km window the ordinal edge shows all four values and the
climate edge shows **one** value.  That is a sample fact about that window and
seed; this script makes **no** universal claim that no window anywhere can hold
all 16 slots, and it never reports the independent direct product as if it were a
co-located observation.

What is read, and what is never touched
---------------------------------------

Read (``verification/`` is opened read-only and stays byte-identical):

* ``verification/metric-region-v1/literal_metre/landforms.npz`` keys ``weights``
  (float64 (509, 509, 4)) and ``dominant_type`` (uint8 (509, 509)) with
  ``np.load(..., allow_pickle=False)``;
* ``verification/metric-region-v1/literal_metre/base/manifest.json`` for the grid
  geometry and seed;
* the 16 biome json **names** under
  ``src/main/resources/data/remotemountains/worldgen/biome`` (existence only).

Consumed, never modified: ``terrain_pipeline/surface_rivers/metric_biome_climate.py``
(the frozen P5.2 rules), ``terrain_pipeline/surface_rivers/metric_climate_refinement.py``
(v2 climate, P4 delivered) and -- for the co-located section only --
``terrain_pipeline/metric_region.py`` with ``terrain_pipeline/hydrology_planning.py``,
through their public entry points.  Nothing is written under ``verification/``.

Where the normalized numbers come from (§2.1, zero new assumptions):
``temperature = clip((BIO1_c + 12) / 45, 0, 1)`` and ``rain = clip(BIO12_mm / 2200, 0, 1)``,
implemented once in ``metric_biome_climate.climate_coordinates``; both are
**normalized biome-selection coordinates, not physical climate quantities**.

Run:

    .\runtime\venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\verify_biome_climate_distribution.py

modules.purpose:
Read-only pillar-field true-3D bundles for the local review UI.

This is the volume-form companion of ``special_surface``.  The height-field study of
``kind == "sandstone_pillar_field"`` cannot express a multi-sided polygonal prism section,
a vertical wall, an outward-bulging iron cap or a wall alcove, so the L1 module
``terrain_pipeline.special_terrain_pillars3d`` supersedes those field values with a real
closed MESH64 solid.  Nothing here advances physics, writes a routing graph or certifies a
channel: the artifact's own ``status`` is ``candidate`` and all six capability flags stay
false.

Pinning follows ``special_surface`` exactly: the report is pinned by its own SHA256 *and*
its identity, and both mesh archives are pinned by digest, so a metadata edit cannot
quietly re-point the viewer at different bytes.

Mesh arrays ship as one JSON descriptor plus separate little-endian binary bodies: the
vertex blob is the stored local-frame vertices, and the triangle blob is the stored
``triangles``.  Topology is therefore *reused*, never rebuilt, and the frontend hands both
straight to ``THREE.BufferAttribute``.

modules.purpose:
Read-only special-terrain surface bundles for the local review UI.

A chart in this package is a *synthetic analytic* landform study, not a georeferenced
landscape: the four bundles are pinned by a manifest that carries each archive's digest
and identity, and the reader refuses to touch a file whose digest or identity has moved.
Nothing here advances physics, writes a routing graph or certifies a channel -- the four
capability flags stay false, and the display is an illustration of stored arrays.

The manifest is pinned by its own SHA256 as well, so a *metadata* edit to a bundle entry
cannot quietly re-point a case at a different archive: adding a form means re-pinning the
manifest constant, which is a deliberate source change rather than a silent one.  This is
the same shape as ``saved_surface.ACCEPTANCE_SHA``, one level down.

Mesh arrays are shipped as one JSON descriptor plus separate binary bodies, following
``saved_surface``: the vertex blob is the stored ``vertices_xyz_m`` minus its own AABB
minimum, and the triangle index blob is the stored ``triangles``.  Topology is therefore
*reused*, never rebuilt, and the frontend can hand both straight to ``THREE.BufferAttribute``.
